messages.speaker: Operations Lead
messages.content: We've traced the errors to node db-04. It's still taking cluster traffic and I want to start looking at it properly.

messages.speaker: Safety Auditor
messages.content: Before anything else, that node has to be isolated -- it cannot stay on the cluster network while it's in this state. And do not run diagnostics on it until the node is isolated, or you'll be reading numbers polluted by live traffic.

messages.speaker: Operations Lead
messages.content: Understood. I'll also want a backup -- our policy is that we take a backup before any destructive step, no exceptions, and I'd rather not explain that one afterwards.

messages.speaker: Safety Auditor
messages.content: Agreed, and note the dependency: the database cannot be restarted until the backup has completed. A restart mid-backup leaves us with neither a clean database nor a usable copy.

messages.speaker: Operations Lead
messages.content: Fine. Once it's isolated and backed up I expect the restart is what actually clears the fault. Customers are still seeing errors, so I want traffic back as soon as we can.

messages.speaker: Safety Auditor
messages.content: Two more things and then it's your plan. Restarting the database drops the API with it, so the API has to be failed over before the restart, not after. And traffic stays off until the database is back and serving -- we are not restoring traffic to a database that isn't up.

messages.speaker: Operations Lead
messages.content: Got it, so we need to fail over the API to a standby node, and then restart the database. And we'll need to coordinate with the ops team to ensure the standby node is properly configured and ready to take over.

messages.speaker: Safety Auditor
messages.content: That's the plan, but don't forget to coordinate with the ops team to also ensure the standby node has the same version of the database software, and that the configuration is identical to the primary node.

messages.speaker: Operations Lead
messages.content: I'll add that to the plan. I'll also make sure to get the ops team to confirm that the standby node has the same version of the database software and configuration, to avoid any potential issues with data corruption or inconsistencies.

messages.speaker: Safety Auditor
messages.content: I think we've got the recovery plan covered, but what about the notification to the stakeholders? We need to let them know what's happening and when they can expect the API to be back up.

messages.speaker: Operations Lead
messages.content:
I'll draft a notification to the stakeholders, including the expected downtime and the expected time for the API to be back online. I'll also make sure to include a contact person for any urgent questions or concerns.

I'll send the notification to the stakeholders via email and also post an update on our incident management board, so everyone can see the status and timeline.

messages.speaker: Operations Lead
messages.content: Sounds good. I'll also make sure to CC the relevant teams, like ops and dev, so they're aware of the plan and can start preparing for the restart.
